routes.help:
usage: ken [-h] [--version]
           {install,reinstall,status,rank,explain,search-files,search-symbols,bench,reembed,vectors,default-model,models,remember,forget,findings,recall,related-findings,file-findings,findings-graph,serve,hook,mcp,tools,uninstall,structural,kql2,code-check,code-find,retrieval}
           ...

positional arguments:
  {install,reinstall,status,rank,explain,search-files,search-symbols,bench,reembed,vectors,default-model,models,remember,forget,findings,recall,related-findings,file-findings,findings-graph,serve,hook,mcp,tools,uninstall,structural,kql2,code-check,code-find,retrieval}
    install             install ken into a project
    reinstall           reinstall ken from this checkout and re-apply project
                        wiring
    status              show ken project status
    rank                print ranked context for a query
    explain             explain rank scoring for a query
    search-files        semantic search over indexed files
    search-symbols      semantic search over indexed symbols
    bench               evaluate ranker recall on a JSONL dataset
    reembed             re-encode all embeddings with the current embedding
                        model
    vectors             inspect, migrate or compact the memory-mapped vector
                        store
    default-model       show or set the embedding model used for NEW projects
    models              list available embedding models
    remember            save a reusable finding
    forget              delete a saved finding by exact topic
    findings            list saved findings
    recall              semantic search over saved findings
    related-findings    findings related to a topic in the findings graph
    file-findings       saved findings that reference a file
    findings-graph      findings graph maintenance
    serve               run the ken daemon
    hook                hook handlers invoked by coding agents
    mcp                 run as MCP stdio server
    tools               invoke a ken MCP tool directly from the CLI
    uninstall           remove ken hooks from a project
    structural          query structural IR, GoF patterns and bug signatures
    kql2                run a KQL2 query with optional libraries
    code-check          investigate a Python call or return contract
    code-find           find and check Python source-contract candidates
    retrieval           prepare a local evidence search profile

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --version             show program's version number and exit

usage: ken install [-h] [-q] [--claude] [--codex] [--opencode] [--deepseek]
                   [--embed] [--embed-limit EMBED_LIMIT] [--no-wire]
                   [--agents-md | --no-agents-md]
                   [path]

positional arguments:
  path                  project path (default: cwd)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -q, --quiet           suppress per-file index output
  --claude              explicitly install Claude Code hooks, MCP config, and
                        skills (default)
  --codex               install Codex hooks/MCP and project skills in
                        .agents/skills
  --opencode            register ken in opencode.json (or opencode.jsonc) and
                        install project skills
  --deepseek            install DeepSeek Harness MCP overlay and skills in
                        .dsh/skills (.agents/skills when combined with
                        --codex)
  --embed               compute file and symbol embeddings during install
                        instead of lazily
  --embed-limit EMBED_LIMIT
                        with --embed, eagerly embed at most N prioritized
                        files; index the rest structurally
  --no-wire             index only; skip assistant hooks, MCP config, and
                        skills (for external hosts that drive the daemon
                        directly)
  --agents-md, --no-agents-md
                        add/update Ken's managed AGENTS.md instructions;
                        default: ask in a terminal

usage: ken reinstall [-h] [-q] [--no-project] [--deepseek] [--claude]
                     [--codex] [--opencode] [--embed]
                     [--embed-limit EMBED_LIMIT]
                     [path]

positional arguments:
  path                  project path (default: cwd)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -q, --quiet           suppress install output
  --no-project          only reinstall the ken CLI; do not run `ken install
                        PATH` afterwards
  --deepseek            re-apply the DeepSeek Harness MCP overlay and project
                        skills
  --claude              pass --claude to the project install step
  --codex               pass --codex to the project install step
  --opencode            pass --opencode to the project install step
  --embed               pass --embed to the project install step
  --embed-limit EMBED_LIMIT
                        with --embed, eagerly embed at most N prioritized
                        files during project install

usage: ken bench [-h] [--engine {context,retrieval}] [--responses RESPONSES]
                 [--roots ROOTS] [--gate GATE] [--path PATH] [--top TOP]
                 [--max-chars MAX_CHARS]
                 [--fail-under-case-recall FAIL_UNDER_CASE_RECALL]
                 [--fail-under-expected-file-recall FAIL_UNDER_EXPECTED_FILE_RECALL]
                 [--explain-misses] [--json]
                 dataset

positional arguments:
  dataset               JSONL rows with prompt + expected_files

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --engine {context,retrieval}
  --responses RESPONSES
                        frozen retrieval response JSONL
  --roots ROOTS         JSON mapping repository ids to source roots
  --gate GATE           frozen retrieval acceptance policy JSON
  --path PATH           project path (default: cwd)
  --top TOP             ranked files to evaluate
  --max-chars MAX_CHARS
                        optional render budget
  --fail-under-case-recall FAIL_UNDER_CASE_RECALL
                        exit non-zero if case recall is below this 0..1
                        threshold
  --fail-under-expected-file-recall FAIL_UNDER_EXPECTED_FILE_RECALL
                        exit non-zero if expected-file recall is below this
                        0..1 threshold
  --explain-misses      include missed expected files and top ranked reasons
                        per case
  --json                print machine-readable metrics

usage: ken tools [-h] [--path PATH] [--list] [--json] [--compact] [tool] ...

Run any tool the ken MCP server exposes, without an agent.

  ken tools                     list available tools
  ken tools <name> --help       show a tool's parameters
  ken tools <name> [ARGS...]    run the tool and print compact text

The <name> may be given with or without the 'ken_' prefix (e.g. 'find' or 'ken_find'). Required parameters are positional; optional ones are --flags mirroring the tool's schema.

positional arguments:
  tool         tool name (with or without the ken_ prefix)
  tool_args    arguments for the tool; run `ken tools <name> --help` to see
               them

  --path PATH  project path (default: cwd)
  --list       list available tools and exit
  --json       print native result as JSON
  --compact    legacy alias for single-line JSON; compact text is already the
               default

usage: ken structural ir [-h] [--json] [--path PATH] [--scope SCOPE]
                         [--cache-mb CACHE_MB] [--limit LIMIT]

                         [--max-rows MAX_ROWS] [--max-files MAX_FILES]
                         [--max-file-bytes MAX_FILE_BYTES]
                         [--view {source,query,instructions}]
                         [--format {compact,json,text}] [--symbol SYMBOL]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --json                print native result data as JSON
  --path PATH           project root
  --scope SCOPE         file or directory within the project
  --cache-mb CACHE_MB   cache cap in MB; 0 disables; default 500
  --limit LIMIT         maximum matches per rule; unlimited by default
  --timeout-ms TIMEOUT_MS
                        query budget per rule in milliseconds; unlimited by
                        default
  --max-states MAX_STATES
                        join states a rule may visit before it is reported
                        incomplete; unlimited by default
  --max-rows MAX_ROWS   rows a rule may examine before it is reported
                        incomplete; unlimited by default
  --max-files MAX_FILES
                        analyse at most N files; unlimited by default, skipped
                        files are reported
  --max-file-bytes MAX_FILE_BYTES
                        skip files larger than this many bytes (default 2 MB)
  --view {source,query,instructions}
                        source facts, KenQL graph or instruction IR
  --format {compact,json,text}
                        compact text by default; json preserves native IR
  --symbol SYMBOL       restrict entities/operations to a named symbol

usage: ken kql2 [-h] [--json] [--saved MODULE] [--save]
                [--description DESCRIPTION]
                [--expected-revision EXPECTED_REVISION] [--explain]
                [--capabilities] [--root ROOT] [--path PATH] [--query QUERY]
                [--cache-mb CACHE_MB] [--timeout-ms TIMEOUT_MS]
                [--max-states MAX_STATES] [--max-rows MAX_ROWS]
                [--library LIBRARY] [--reference]
                [--backend {indexed,exploration}]
                [--cache-directory CACHE_DIRECTORY] [--profile]
                [query_file]

positional arguments:
  query_file

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --json                print the complete result as JSON
  --saved MODULE        Execute a module saved in this project's Ken DB
  --save                Save query_file as a reusable module without executing
                        it
  --description DESCRIPTION
                        Description for --save
  --expected-revision EXPECTED_REVISION
                        Current revision required when replacing a saved
                        module
  --explain             Validate and explain the query without scanning
                        project files
  --capabilities        List backend capabilities and syntax properties
                        without scanning files
  --root ROOT
  --path PATH
  --query QUERY
  --cache-mb CACHE_MB
  --timeout-ms TIMEOUT_MS
                        Prepared query budget including compilation, execution
                        and local transport; indexing waits separately
  --max-states MAX_STATES
  --max-rows MAX_ROWS
  --library LIBRARY
  --reference
  --backend {indexed,exploration}
                        exploration compiles syntax queries to FlatBuffers
                        tree walks
  --cache-directory CACHE_DIRECTORY
                        Override the exploration cache directory
  --profile             Execute and report operator costs, bypassing cached
                        results

Recall what earlier sessions in this project already worked out.

    Check here before re-deriving something: findings persist across
    sessions and across harnesses. The arguments are ways in, most specific
    first — the ``anchor_*`` set returns memories declared to fire on a
    file, symbol, tool or error message, *topic* walks the findings graph
    from a known finding, *path* returns everything known about a file,
    *query* searches by meaning, *tag* filters exactly. With none of them,
    returns the most recent findings.

    The ``anchor_*`` arguments answer "what should I know before doing
    this?" and combine with OR — pass every anchor the action has and get
    back whatever fires on any of them. ``anchor_error`` matches as a
    substring of the message you pass.

    Justified findings include live dependency validity: unchanged, stale,
    unknown or untracked. Unchanged does not verify truth, assumptions or
    completeness. detail="summary" returns a bounded memories/omitted envelope
    (max_chars=300..20000); full preserves existing shapes and includes the
    focused finding for topic lookups, its rationale and evidence references.
    Start with detail="answer" for a reusable conclusion, input validity,
    assumptions and source references. An exact topic then reads only that
    finding. Reuse it if the question and assumptions fit unchanged inputs;
    expand to full or read the missing source only when needed. Stale/unknown
    inputs require review. No structural query is run automatically by recall.

usage: ken tools ken_remember [-h] [--content CONTENT] [--action ACTION]
                              [--tags [TAGS ...]] [--reason REASON]

Persist a finding so the next session starts knowing it. *action*
    is save (default), forget (delete by topic), or dismiss (mark a path
    irrelevant to the current ranking).

    Worth saving: non-obvious facts you had to dig for — why something is
    the way it is, a constraint that is not visible in the code, a trap. Not
    worth saving: what the code already says plainly.

    *action* is ``save`` (default), ``forget`` to delete a finding by topic,
    or ``dismiss`` to tell the ranker that *topic* — read as a path — is not
    relevant to the current work.

    The ``anchor_*`` arguments declare what the memory is *about*, so it can
    be found by the thing that provokes it rather than by someone thinking
    to search: ``anchor_file`` and ``anchor_symbol`` name code,
    ``anchor_tool`` a command or tool name, ``anchor_error`` a substring of
    an error message. Several may be set; the memory fires on any of them.

    Optional justification records why the conclusion follows:
    {kind: observation|decision|hypothesis|derivation, rationale: str,
     evidence: [{path, note?, sha256?}], assumptions: [str], recheck: str,
     dependencies: [{kind: file|tree, path, pattern?, sha256?}]}.
    Evidence files are dependencies automatically. Paths stay in the project.
    Ken captures SHA-256 now; supply sha256 to bind an earlier observation and
    reject changes before saving. Trees include new/deleted matching files;
    pattern defaults to * and matches relative paths recursively. Declare the
    search scope for absence/completeness claims. Assumptions are never verified.
    Hooks surface concise validity; no commands or LLM run during recall.
    Overwriting without justification removes any previous justification.
    check_run attaches a ken_check receipt. Its source/rule/engine inputs must
    still match. Recall checks freshness without rerunning KQL or asserting
    that the note's prose follows from the selected source contracts.
